action_items: Marcus Lee - run 10k sample with batch size 8 and kv cache warmup script - due 2026-03-30
Priya Nair - share canonical prompts and golden answers - due 2026-03-29

transcript:
Header: 2026-03-25 14:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Diego (CS), Priya (Cordata ML), Ethan (Cordata Platform), Sofia (Cordata Data)

Auto-summary: quick bench retro, we compared p95/p99 and throughput vs CurrentVendorX baseline, identified tail spikes on long context, proposed batching and cache changes, agreed on next runs and security deep-dive.

[00:00:05] Ava: okay everyone welcome, thanks for joining the sprint bench retro, we wanted to go over the numbers from last week's runs and figure out tuning and next steps.
[00:00:18] Priya: yeah thanks, we had a couple outages on the vendor side so appreciate that you could get the batch runs in, quick heads up we are mostly focused on 512 token qa style queries which is, um, our most frequent path.
[00:00:32] Marcus: understood, the test harness matched your shape, we used the same tokenization and prompt templates, slight difference in sampling but should be negligible.
[00:00:45] Ethan: one note, the baseline we shared earlier is CurrentVendorX using 80GB A100s with dynamic batching at 16, quant int8 for the model.
[00:01:02] Sofia: and we also measure p50/p95/p99 and tail latency, plus requests per second for throughput.
[00:01:17] Diego: quick logistics, i'll drop the raw csvs and the plotted graphs in the slack channel after the call.
[00:01:30] Priya: great. can we start with the p95 comparisons?
[00:01:36] Marcus: sure, so slide one, p95 for 512 tokens: Redwood (hosted) median p95 = 220ms vs baseline 310ms, p99 520ms vs baseline 890ms. these are from a 1k-run with concurrency 5.
[00:02:02] Priya: wait p99 520, is that with kv cache enabled?
[00:02:08] Marcus: yes, kv cache warmed for about 20% of the requests, we saw cache hit rates affecting p99 significantly.
[00:02:20] Ethan: interesting, our vendor had higher cache miss rates and we saw long KV regeneration spikes. how predictable is your cache warming in prod?
[00:02:33] Marcus: that's a good question — we have a prefix cache and proactive warm strategies, but for the pilot we used conservative warm limits to avoid heavy memory. we can increase warm window for these flows.
[00:02:47] Priya: any difference when batching increases? we noticed p95 dropped but p99 got weird.
[00:02:54] Marcus: yes, as we increased batch size from 1 to 8 p50/p95 improved linearly but p99 showed some outliers due to long-tail lock contention and token-rematerialization for very long sequences.
[00:03:12] Ava: to be clear, baseline vendor does more aggressive batching and sometimes trades latency for throughput, which matches what you're seeing.
[00:03:23] Priya: right that's our worry, we want predictable tails.
[00:03:29] Marcus: we can tune the runtime to cap batch build time and opt for smaller max-batch for latency-sensitive routes. also the runtime has a mode for latency-first vs throughput-first.
[00:03:42] Sofia: can you explain the latency-first mode? I didn't see that in the doc.
[00:03:46] Marcus: yeah it's a scheduler knob; it prioritizes starting smaller batches earlier and falls back to single-request fast-paths, reduces variance but lowers aggregate throughput.
[00:03:58] Ethan: do we lose cost efficiency with latency-first?
[00:04:02] Marcus: slightly, but the Optimize toolkit can quantify that — we estimated +8–12% cost per token for the latency-first config on this workload.
[00:04:15] Priya: acceptable if tails are stable. what's the throughput difference?
[00:04:19] Marcus: at concurrency 10, Redwood sustained ~1,800 RPS for 512 tokens with batch size 4 average, baseline was ~2,200 RPS but with p99 at 1.2s.
[00:04:36] Priya: so baseline better raw RPS but worse p99. that matches internal complaints.
[00:04:42] Ava: exactly, the tradeoff is cost+latency predictability.
[00:04:48] [00:06:05] (crosstalk, brief)
[00:06:20] Sofia: about the KV cache hit patterns, we saw your notes referencing prefix cache vs full-kv, can we get more detail?
[00:06:29] Marcus: in this test we used prefix cache keyed on prompt signature; if prompts vary too much the hit rate drops. We recommended normalizing prompts and adding a small canonicalization layer.
[00:06:44] Priya: we'll try to canonicalize, that should help.
[00:06:52] Ethan: security question — for private deployment, how does KMS integration look? we need BYOK with HSM.
[00:07:00] Ava: Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs; we'll send the SOC2/ISO docs and the integration checklist after.
[00:07:10] Priya: perfect, can we see the audit log retention window?
[00:07:14] Ava: yes, default is 90d but enterprise packages can extend to 365d.
[00:07:20] Priya: okay.
[00:07:25] Marcus: back to performance, we ran a mixed-concurrency test (1/5/10) that simulates bursty traffic; Redwood's tail improved when we enabled KV pre-warm for the 1 path but the 10-concurrency path still hit p99 spikes around 600ms.
[00:07:44] Priya: do those spikes correlate with garbage collection or GPU memory pressure?
[00:07:49] Marcus: more with scheduling delays and occasional kernel path fallbacks; the runtime will swap execution kernels for some sequence lengths which causes a small hiccup. we can pin kernel variants for consistency.
[00:08:04] Ethan: can we get a run with pinned kernels and heavier warmup? that would show more comparable p99 numbers.
[00:08:11] Marcus: yes we can do that in next iteration.
[00:08:17] [00:09:30] Priya: also quality — we haven't seen regressions but need a golden set. we'll send that.
[00:09:38] Ava: appreciated. Diego will also prepare a short how-to for the warmup script and a sample Docker job you can run to reproduce locally.
[00:09:49] Diego: yep i'll upload that and link it.
[00:10:05] Sofia: can you share the cost delta estimates for dedicated slots? we need a ballpark for infra planning.
[00:10:12] Ava: for an 8-slot dedicated pool with mixed GPUs we estimated monthly $Xk — i'll send the spreadsheet, but rough delta vs baseline depends on utilization; if you hit 70% util the unit cost is favorable.
[00:10:28] Priya: what's the onboarding timeline to migrate pilot to Private? we have security review next month.
[00:10:35] Ava: Private onboarding typically 4–6 weeks for a VPC deployment, less if you go with Redwood-hosted dedicated. the security deep-dive will be useful to nail this down.
[00:10:46] Ethan: ok we'll aim for the week of Apr 6 for the deep-dive.
[00:10:52] Marcus: quick note: we observed a specific long-tail pattern with prompts that contain long code blocks; those trigger longer attention kernels, causing the p99 to spike. a preprocessor to trim irrelevant code could help.
[00:11:08] Priya: yes, we'll add a sanitize step and low confidence fallback.
[00:11:15] [00:12:45] (discussion about run reproducibility and seed handling)
[00:13:10] Marcus: small gotcha — sampling randomness can produce variance; for latency bench use deterministic sampling config to reduce noise.
[00:13:21] Priya: good point.
[00:13:27] Ava: let's confirm the next run matrix: 1) deterministic sampling, 2) pinned kernel, 3) kv pre-warm full for the 1k set, 4) mixed concurrency 1/5/10. Marcus will run and post results.
[00:13:45] Priya: sounds good.
[00:13:49] [00:15:00] (brief pause, off-topic jokes)
[00:15:20] Ethan: procurement question — contract windows and early termination for pilot?
[00:15:25] Ava: for pilots we offer monthly with 30-day opt-out; Dedicated requires minimum 90-day notice for decommissioning in our draft terms, but we'll send legal templates.
[00:15:40] Priya: okay.
[00:16:02] Marcus: another tuning lever is model quant profile; for your workload int8 gave good perf, but we can try q4f16 hybrid for a balance of quality and speed.
[00:16:14] Sofia: any expected quality delta?
[00:16:17] Marcus: small, often negligible on QA tasks, but we should run evals against your golden set.
[00:16:27] Priya: we'll prioritize that in the next run.
[00:16:36] [00:18:10] (discussion of sharing dashboards and traces)
[00:18:25] Diego: i'll push a dashboard with token-level cost and latency breakdown by model variant, link in slack.
[00:18:33] Priya: seeing traces will help debug those p99 spikes.
[00:18:38] Ava: yes we can grant limited console access for engineering.
[00:18:42] Ethan: who from Redwood will attend the security deep-dive?
[00:18:45] Ava: Marcus, Diego, and I; plus our security engineer if needed.
[00:18:52] Priya: good.
[00:19:05] Marcus: any blockers from Cordata on running the next matrix?
[00:19:10] Priya: only the golden set and the vendor config; we'll get those to you this week.
[00:19:17] Ava: excellent.
[00:19:23] [00:21:00] (mid-call recap)
[00:21:15] Ava: recap: Marcus runs pinned-kernel + prewarm + deterministic sampling; Priya provides golden prompts; Ava sends pricing and security docs; Diego uploads warmup scripts and dashboards.
[00:21:30] Priya: timeline looks good.
[00:21:35] Ethan: can we also ask for a short run that simulates our nightly batch of 250k requests? just to get cost projection.
[00:21:44] Marcus: yes we can approximate that, will include in the cost model.
[00:21:50] [00:23:49] (some small clarifications, misc)
[00:24:05] Sofia: one more thing, the vendor uses a custom ontoken caching layer, how does your cache compare?
[00:24:12] Marcus: ours is prefix-first; their approach is sometimes better for certain prompt families. we can experiment if you provide a representative sample.
[00:24:25] Priya: will do.
[00:24:33] Ava: any other questions?
[00:24:37] Priya: none from me.
[00:24:40] Ethan: none.
[00:24:42] Sofia: nope.
[00:24:45] Ava: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the files and the scheduled deep-dive invite.
[00:24:52] [00:25:00] (meeting ends, small outro)

Notes: CSVs and plots to be uploaded to slack channel #cordata-pilot; watch for the 'pinned-kernel' tag in filenames.
